subject: Can I conduct spatial modeling when one covariate is categorical?

messages.author: 82a29501c95feac5
messages.subject: Can I conduct spatial modeling when one covariate is categorical?
parts:
Hi all,

I want to model distribution of geochemical element concentration using INLA-SPDE.  One of the covariate for modeling fixed effect is categorical. 

I followed the strategy as in classical regression, i.e. converting the categorical covariate into several dummy variables, and kept part of them for modeling.

The following is a screenshot of the preprocessed data, the dummy varaibles being indicated by columns of "Lithos" and "Intrus" (part of the complete data file named "geochem.csv" with 623 lines):


The following is my code:

library(INLA)
## -----------prepare data --------------
rawdata<-read.table('geochem.csv', sep=",", header=TRUE, encoding="UTF-8")
coo<-rawdata[, c("X", "Y")] 
coo<-as.matrix(coo)
x1 <- rawdata[, "Faults"]
x2 <- rawdata[, "Lithos"]
x3 <- rawdata[, "Intrus"]
y<-rawdata[, "RPC2"]

## ------ Modeling with INLA ------------
# 1. Mesh
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  coo,
  max.edge=c(0.1, 0.2),
  cutoff=0.005)
plot(mesh, asp=1); points(coo, col='red', cex=0.5)

# 2. Define the projector matrix
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh, loc=coo)

# 3. Build the SPDE model on the mesh
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(
  mesh=mesh, alpha=1.5)

# 4. Create a stack data
stk.e <- inla.stack(tag='est',
                    data=list(y=y),
                    A=list(A, 1),
                    effects=list(
                      s=1:spde$n.spde,
                      data.frame(b0=1, x1=x1, x2=x2, x3=x3)))

# 5. Fit
formula <- y ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + x3
  f(s, model=spde) ## RF term
res <- inla(formula, data=inla.stack.data(stk.e),
            control.predictor=list(A = inla.stack.A(stk.e)))# projector

res$summary.fixed

Now my questions are:
(1) whether my code is right for dealing with the dummy variables, especially the lines of defining "inla.stack";
(2) whether do I need to normalize the continuous covariate "Faults" into the range of [0, 1] before inla modeling?
(3) the coordinates x, y have been translated and scaled into [0, 1], so whether the parameters "max.edge" and "cutoff" are correctly set when building the mesh?

Is there anyone that could give me a help? Thank you.

Best regards,
Kuan

messages.author: 74f2e6fef4c447fd
messages.subject: Re: Can I conduct spatial modeling when one covariate is categorical?
parts:
This looks fine to me. You could compare your code with this tutorial that shows how to build a similar model with inla versus inlabru: https://www.muscardinus.be/2018/07/inlabru-bru/

Q1: the stack statement looks OK to me, but I am not sure about the A=list(A, 1) and b0=1 at the same time. Hopefully someone else can check that -- this part always confuses me.

Q2: you don't have to center or scale the continuous covariate if you don't want. but there are advantages to doing it related to computing stability and setting/understanding priors and interpreting coefficients. E.g., Andrew Gelman has a paper on scaling continuous and categorical variables so that beta coefficients are comparable.

Q3: if the mesh and data are all on a consistently scaled coordinate system, you should be fine. the only exception is if some functions that you use downstream in your analysis are looking for a consistent CRS. you might get errors that crs's don't match.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Can I conduct spatial modeling when one covariate is categorical?
parts:
Good answers from Tim!

I’ll add that the b0=1 part is fine, since the data.frame will expand it to an all-1 column matching the lengths of the other columns.

From the visible values of the continuous covariate, I would recommend not scaling it, since it’s already on a decent scale. In any case, scaling based on empirical variance etc should be avoided, since it’s so fragile with respect to data subsampling and other data set changes, such as for spatial prediction. When/if scaling is needed for numerical reasons, I would instead recommend choosing the scaling by hand (e.g. as a whole power of 10).

Finn
